scope: Primary breast evidence only; clinician card endpoints, not personalised prognosis

00232.name: GEICAM 2000-04
00232.design: Randomised phaseIII;252 women with locally recurrent/metastatic breast cancer previously treated with anthracyclines and taxanes.
00232.comparison: Vinorelbine alone versus gemcitabine plus vinorelbine.
00232.schedule_applicability: Monotherapy arm used IVvinorelbine 30 mg/m² Days 1 and 8 every 21 days: exact NCCP 00232 reference schedule.
00232.comparative_results: Adding gemcitabine improved PFS (6.0 versus 4.0 months;HR 0.66,95%CI 0.50–0.88,p=.0028), without an OS difference (15.9 versus 16.4 months;HR 1.04,95%CI 0.78–1.39,p=.8046).
00232.limitations: The comparison evaluates gemcitabine addition; it does not establish an absolute survival benefit from vinorelbine itself. Historical selected breast population; no application to ovarian/lung indications or individual prognosis. Do not compare these medians directly with oral single-arm results.
00232.patient_summary: Vinorelbine has shown activity in advanced breast cancer. Expected benefit depends on cancer biology, earlier treatment and health; historical trial averages do not predict an individual result.

00259.name: Freyer 2003 oral vinorelbine phaseII
00259.citation: Freyer G et al. Journal of Clinical Oncology. 2003;21:35–40. DOI 10.1200/JCO.2003.09.057
00259.design: Single-arm phaseII;64 patients enrolled for first-line chemotherapy of locally advanced/metastatic breast cancer;58 response-evaluable.
00259.schedule_applicability: Oral 60 mg/m² weekly first 3 administrations, then conditional 80 mg/m²: matches NCCP 00259 escalation structure. Trial initially assessed 8 weeks; responding/stable patients continued 12 weeks or longer. Do not make 8 or 12 weeks the NCCP course length.
00259.limitations: Small historical first-line study with response-evaluable analysis; no causal comparative survival claim and no fixed survival estimate. Do not substitute NORBREAST 228 bone-predominant outcomes or its cycle 2 escalation for this schedule. Breast outcomes do not generalise to lung cancer.
00259.patient_summary: The oral weekly schedule has shown activity in advanced breast cancer. It needs blood tests and toxicity review even though capsules are taken at home; oral and IV doses cannot be swapped.
